title: Bootstrap a runnable app shell
user_visible_behavior: The repository has a runnable app with a home route, one install command, one verification command, and one start command, all documented in init.sh.
verification: Run the documented install command from a clean checkout.
Run the documented verification command and confirm it passes.
Start the app and load the home route on a phone-sized viewport.
Replace the provisional commands in init.sh with the real install, verify, and start commands.
evidence: `npm run verify` passed: expo lint, `tsc --noEmit`, and `expo-doctor` 20/20 checks; rerun during independent validation.
`./init.sh` exited 0, ran `npm run verify`, and printed `npm start` without starting the dev server.
`npx expo export --platform android` bundled 1,306 modules successfully.
`CI=1 npx expo start --port 8081` returned Metro status `running`.
Physical Android render verified on Samsung Galaxy M13 (Android 14): Expo Go 58.0.5 displayed `Futsal Manager AI`, the Spanish subtitle, and `Aplicación en construcción` through a `uiautomator` dump.
Fast Refresh verified by changing the home status text on disk and observing the new text on the device; full reload verified by relaunching `exp://127.0.0.1:8081`.

Native debug build verified with `npm run android` (`expo run:android`): Gradle build succeeded, the 60 MB APK installed as `com.anonymous.futsalmanagerai`, and the Spanish home route rendered; Fast Refresh and a force-stop/full relaunch worked in the native app.
Independent validation verdict: accept, with no blocking findings.
notes: Expo SDK 58.0.19, Expo Router, TypeScript. ESLint is pinned to 9 because eslint-config-expo's plugins are incompatible with ESLint 10. `npm run verify` is the standard gate; `npm start` is never run by init.sh. Device loop: docs/device-development-workflow.md. Local debug application ID is the template placeholder `com.anonymous.futsalmanagerai` until a production ID is chosen. Spec: docs/specs/bootstrap-app-shell.md.

title: Define and validate the Board Data schema
user_visible_behavior: An exercise's Board Data (tokens, cones, arrows, labels, ordered phases) validates against a versioned schema, and invalid data is rejected.
verification: Validate a valid multi-phase Board Data fixture and confirm it passes.
Validate fixtures with a missing phase coordinate and an unknown token type; confirm both fail with a clear error.
Record the schema version in the repository.
evidence: Spec created at `docs/specs/board-data-schema.md`; durable contract documented in `docs/board-data-schema.md` with `schemaVersion` `1.0.0`.
Added `zod@4.6.7`, `@types/node@^22`, and `tsx@^4`; `npm test` runs the Board Data suite and `npm run verify` now runs ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`, the schema tests, and `expo-doctor`.

Implemented strict schemas in `src/shared/domain/board-data/schema.ts` for board metadata, tokens, static cones, phases, positions, ball, arrows, and labels, with slug/text/coordinate limits, a literal version, and cross-field refinements.
Implemented `parseBoardData`, `safeParseBoardData`, `BoardDataValidationError`, and dot-notation issue paths in `src/shared/domain/board-data/index.ts`.
Created a prototype-derived three-phase valid fixture and four invalid fixtures (missing position, unknown token kind, unknown version, unexpected field).

`npm test`: 12/12 pass, covering valid parsing, defaults, per-phase token completeness, half-pitch data, missing position, unknown kind, unknown version, strict extra field, phase order, unknown token position, and thrown error formatting.

Missing-position fixture reports `phases.1.positions: Missing position for token "ala-izquierda" in phase 2.`; unknown-kind fixture reports `tokens.0.kind: Token kind must be "player" or "keeper".`; version fixture reports `schemaVersion: Board Data schemaVersion must be "1.0.0".`; strict-field fixture reports `(root): Unrecognized key: "notes"`.
`npm run verify` exit 0 with 12/12 schema tests and `expo-doctor` 20/20; `./init.sh` exit 0 and executes the same gate without starting Metro.
`npx expo export --platform android` succeeds after the dependency and tsconfig changes (2.9 MB bundle).
No device verification was required because the feature adds no screen or user-visible behavior.
Independent validation returned `accept` with no blocking findings and was recorded at commit `23ca764` (PR #6 merged to `main` at `9418fde`).

`modular-hexagonal-architecture` moved the unchanged contract, parser, fixtures, and all 12 tests to `src/shared/domain/board-data/` and `tests/shared/domain/board-data/`; `npm test` still passes with `schemaVersion` `1.0.0`.
notes: Board Data v1.0.0 uses normalized 0-100 coordinates on a full 2:1 pitch, board-level tokens and static cones, per-phase positions/ball/arrows/labels, exactly one position per token per phase, strict unknown-key rejection, and no MVP migrations. Rendered with react-native-svg using full keyframe positions per phase, interpolated between phases. The board must preserve a 2:1 pitch ratio. No persistent E2E harness exists; unit tests are the correct coverage level until the renderer and playback exist.

title: Adopt a modular hexagonal architecture
user_visible_behavior: The app keeps its four tabs and design-system gallery unchanged while `src` is organized into business modules with hexagonal layers, shared contracts, public APIs, and mirrored tests.
verification: Inspect `src/modules` and confirm content, board, ai, and club each expose domain, application, infrastructure, presentation, and a public index.ts.
Inspect `src/shared` and confirm Board Data, theme, and UI live there and do not import app routes or business modules.
Open the four tab routes and the design-system gallery and confirm each renders a module screen or shared presentation with no business logic.
Introduce a deliberate cross-module deep import, app-to-module deep import, and shared-to-module import; confirm `npm run lint` rejects each with an architecture message.
Confirm tests mirror the source under `tests/modules`, `tests/shared`, and `tests/architecture`, and behavior tests use Given/When/Then.
Run `npm run verify` and `./init.sh`; confirm lint, typecheck, tests, and expo-doctor pass and the app still starts from the standard path.
Confirm the moved Board Data contract still validates at version 1.0.0 and still rejects invalid data.
evidence: Spec created at `docs/specs/modular-hexagonal-architecture.md`; architecture source of truth created at `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
Created `src/modules/{content,board,ai,club}` with `domain`, `application`, `infrastructure`, `presentation`, a public `index.ts`, and a module `README.md`; empty layers use `.gitkeep`.

Moved Board Data to `src/shared/domain/board-data`, theme to `src/shared/theme`, and UI primitives, layout, and navigation to `src/shared/ui`; `src/components`, `src/content`, and `src/theme` no longer exist.
Rewrote the four tab routes as thin wrappers over `@/modules/<module>` and kept `/design-system` outside the tabs.
Rewrote the 12 Board Data tests as Given/When/Then under `tests/shared/domain/board-data/`; fixtures moved beside them.
Added `tests/architecture/architecture.test.ts` covering the four modules and their layers, all public APIs, shared ownership of board-data/theme/ui, and removal of legacy folders.

Installed `eslint-plugin-boundaries@^7.3.0` and added dependency policies to `eslint.config.js`; deliberate violations produced `Shared code cannot depend on app routes or business modules.`, `Import a module through its public API: @/modules/<module>.`, and `Domain cannot depend on another module; use a shared contract.`
Updated `package.json` so `npm test` discovers `tests/**/*.test.ts` and added `test:watch`; removed `test:board`.
`npm test`: 16/16 pass across 27 suites (12 Board Data + 4 architecture); `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
`npm run verify` exit 0 (lint, typecheck, all tests, expo-doctor 20/20) and `./init.sh` exit 0 without starting Metro.
`npx expo export --platform android` succeeds after the reorg, and the four tabs plus `/design-system` were checked on the connected Samsung Galaxy M13 with no layout or navigation regression.
notes: Modules are business capabilities, not screens or technical folders. Allowed cross-module dependency is `ai -> content`; every module may use `shared`. Board Data is a shared kernel because content, board, and AI all exchange it. Tests mirror the source tree and use Given/When/Then. `npm test` now discovers every test file, so future module tests need no per-feature script. No persistent E2E harness exists; architecture, unit, lint, typecheck, bundle, and device checks are the coverage for a structural feature.
